definition_zh: 感觉；触摸；认为；觉得；触感；直觉
definition_en: to experience an emotion or physical sensation, to touch something, or to hold an opinion; also the sense of touch or a general impression
core_image: 指尖与皮肤成为世界的接口，触到什么、心里就升起什么
scene: 诊室里医生先搓热双手，再为病人检查患处。 The doctor felt the patient's arm gently.
sceneCN: 这里 feel 是动词，指「用手触摸以检查」，对应第 3 个义项；句意为医生轻柔地触按病人的手臂。

derivatives.zh: 感觉；情感（feel 的动名词，指感受或情绪）
感情；情绪（feeling 的复数，多指心情）
触角；试探者（feel 加 -er，指起触觉作用的器官或试探之人）

senses.title: To experience an emotion
senses.definition: to experience a state of mind or emotion
senses.definitionCN: 经历某种心理或情绪状态
senses.example: I feel happy today.
senses.exampleCN: 我今天感到快乐。
senses.why: The inner world is known the way the outer one is touched, so emotion rides on the same verb.
senses.whyCN: 内心世界像外界一样被「摸到」，所以情绪也用同一个动词承载。

senses.title: To sense something physically
senses.definition: to notice something through the body or senses
senses.definitionCN: 通过身体或感官察觉某事
senses.example: She felt a pain in her back.
senses.exampleCN: 她感到背部疼痛。
senses.why: Sensation is the body's data stream, and feel is the verb that reports it.
senses.whyCN: 身体感受是身体的信号流，feel 就是报告它的动词。

senses.title: To touch something
senses.definition: to touch something with the fingers to learn about it
senses.definitionCN: 用手触碰以了解某物
senses.example: He felt the wall for the light switch.
senses.exampleCN: 他在墙上摸电灯开关。
senses.why: The hand searches where the eyes cannot, so the verb moves from sensing to touching.
senses.whyCN: 手在眼睛看不见处搜索，于是动词从「感知」滑向「触摸」。

senses.title: To hold an opinion
senses.definition: to have an opinion or belief about something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事持有看法或信念
senses.example: I feel that the plan is fair.
senses.exampleCN: 我认为这个计划是公平的。
senses.why: An opinion is a judgement you sense before you argue it, so thinking borrows the word.
senses.whyCN: 观点是先于论证被感知到的判断，所以思维借用了这个词。

senses.title: The sense of touch
senses.definition: the ability to feel things through the skin
senses.definitionCN: 通过皮肤感知事物的能力
senses.example: Fingertips give a fine sense of feel.
senses.exampleCN: 指尖提供精细的触觉。
senses.why: The verb freezes into a noun: the act of touching names the faculty itself.
senses.whyCN: 动词凝固为名词：触摸这一行为命名了触觉本身。

senses.title: A general impression or atmosphere
senses.definition: the impression a place or situation gives
senses.definitionCN: 某个地方或情境给人的总体印象
senses.example: The old town has a peaceful feel.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老城给人宁静的感觉。
senses.why: Everything you touch leaves a texture, and a place's mood is its texture.
senses.whyCN: 触过之物都留下质感，一个地方的氛围正是它的质感。

intro.en: Feel is a Germanic strong verb of touch and sensation, whose past tense felt has been stable since Old English.
intro.cn: feel 是日耳曼强变化动词，表触觉与感受，过去式 felt 自古英语以来一直稳定。

items.en: A reconstructed root foljan meant 'to perceive by touch'; related forms appear across Germanic languages.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构词根 foljan 意为「以触觉感知」；相关形式遍布日耳曼诸语。

items.en: Old English felan meant 'to touch, perceive', with the past participle folen.
items.cn: 古英语 felan 意为「触摸、感知」，过去分词为 folen。

items.en: Middle English len kept the strong forms and stretched the verb to emotions.
items.cn: 中古英语继续使用强变化形式，并把动词扩展到情绪领域。

items.en: The verb fixed as feel with felt as past form, covering body, heart and mind.
items.cn: 现代英语定为 feel，过去式 felt，覆盖身体、心灵与思维。

items.en: Modern usage added the noun feel for atmosphere, as in the feel of a place.
items.cn: 现代用法又给名词 feel 增加氛围义，如 the feel of a place。

note.en: Look-alikes differ by one letter; near-meaning words sit in the fields of touch, emotion and opinion.
note.cn: 形近组仅差一个字母；近义组分布于触觉、情绪与看法三个义场。

abstract.en: Emotions are touches that never reach the hand.

examples.en: She felt the fabric before buying the coat.

examples.en: I feel that we should leave early to avoid traffic.
examples.cn: 我觉得我们该早点出发避开堵车。

definition_zh: 再一次；又；回到原处；此外
definition_en: one more time, or back to a former place or state
core_image: 雨停了一会儿又下起来
scene: 雨停了一会儿，又下了起来。 The rain started again.
sceneCN: 这里 again 是「再一次」（第 1 个义项：又一次发生）；句意为雨又下起来了。

pos.zh: 副词：再一次；又；回到原处；此外

senses.title: One more time
senses.definition: one more time
senses.definitionCN: 再做一次
senses.example: Please say that again.
senses.exampleCN: 请再说一遍。
senses.why: The old word meant back or in the opposite direction, and a repeated act is a return to the same point.
senses.whyCN: 古词意为「返回、逆向」，重复做一件事就是回到同一点，因此是再一次。

senses.title: Back to a place
senses.definition: back to a place one had left
senses.definitionCN: 回到离开过的地方
senses.example: She came home again.
senses.exampleCN: 她又回家了。
senses.why: The spatial sense of coming back survives in the sense of returning to a place.
senses.whyCN: 「回来」的空间义保留下来，就是回到原处。

senses.title: As a further point
senses.definition: used to add another point in speech
senses.definitionCN: 在说话时补充另一点
senses.example: Again, the price has risen.
senses.exampleCN: 再说，价格又上涨了。
senses.why: Turning the talk back to add a point gives the spoken sense of again.
senses.whyCN: 把话头转回来再补一点，就是口语里的「再说」。

definition_en: a person who helps another in their work, or a person who serves customers
core_image: 教室里助教把一摞书发给学生
scene: 教室里，助教把一摞书逐本发给学生。 The teacher's assistant handed out the books.

senses.exampleCN: 老师的助教把书发了下去。

definition_en: to examine something to make sure it is right or safe; to stop something; a bill or written order to pay
core_image: 落子前先停一停，把每一步都看清楚再放行
scene: 交卷之前，班长提醒大家先核对一遍名字和题号。 Please check your answers before you hand in the paper.
sceneCN: 这里 check 是「检查；核对」（第 1 个义项：查验以确保无误）；句意为交卷前请先核对答案。

derivatives.zh: 由 check 加 -er 构成，义为「检查员；检验器」
由 check 加 out 构成，义为「结账处；检验」
由 check 加 list 构成，义为「核对清单」

senses.title: To examine to make sure all is right
senses.definition: to look at something carefully to be sure it is correct, safe or complete
senses.definitionCN: 仔细查看以确保正确、安全或完整
senses.example: Please check your answers before handing in the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 交卷前请核对答案。
senses.why: The chess call for a threat made players look twice, and looking twice became examining anything carefully.
senses.whyCN: 象棋中「将军」的喊声让人反复确认，反复确认便成了仔细查验。

senses.title: To stop something from growing or moving
senses.definition: to hold something back so it cannot grow or move freely
senses.definitionCN: 牵制某物，使其不能自由增长或行动
senses.example: The fence checks the wind across the field.
senses.exampleCN: 围栏挡住了田野上的风。
senses.why: In chess, a checked king cannot move freely; anything held back by a threat is likewise checked.
senses.whyCN: 象棋里被将军的王寸步难行；被威胁所牵制之物同样被「将」住了。

senses.title: A written order to pay money
senses.definition: a printed form telling a bank to pay money from your account
senses.definitionCN: 通知银行从账户付款的印制单据
senses.example: Grandpa paid the fee by cheque.
senses.exampleCN: 爷爷用支票付了费用。
senses.why: A bank paper 'checks' the account: it calls for the money to be examined and handed over.
senses.whyCN: 银行单据「查验」账户：要求核对后将款项交付。

senses.title: A bill in a restaurant
senses.definition: the written bill for food or services in a restaurant
senses.definitionCN: 餐馆里写明餐费的单据
senses.example: Let me see the check, please.
senses.exampleCN: 请把账单给我看看。
senses.why: The bill is the paper that lets you examine and settle what you owe.
senses.whyCN: 账单就是让你核对并结清所欠款项的那张纸。

senses.title: A pattern of squares, or a mark of correctness
senses.definition: a pattern of crossed squares, or a mark showing something has been examined
senses.definitionCN: 交叉的方格图案，或表示已查验的记号
senses.example: The teacher put a check beside each correct answer.
senses.exampleCN: 老师在每道正确答案旁打了勾。
senses.why: Marking an examined item with a tick, like squares on a board, fixes the examining sense into a visible sign.
senses.whyCN: 用记号标注已查过的项目，如同棋盘上的方格，把查验之义固定成可见的符号。

intro.en: Check comes from the game of chess: the call shah, 'the king is threatened', travelled through Persian into everyday English.
intro.cn: check 源自国际象棋：波斯语的「王被将」呼语一路传入日常英语。

items.en: Persian shah means king; shah mat gave the chess phrase for a trapped king.
items.cn: 波斯语 shah 意为国王；shah mat 是棋语中被困之王的呼语。

items.en: Old French eschec meant the call in chess and any setback or check.
items.cn: 古法语 eschec 指象棋中的将军呼语，也指挫败。

items.en: Middle English chek kept the chess sense and grew the sense of stopping or rebuke.
items.cn: 中古英语 chek 保留棋义，并发展出阻止、惩戒之义。

items.en: Senses multiplied: examining, controlling, bank cheques, square patterns.
items.cn: 义项倍增：查验、控制、银行支票、方格图案。

items.en: American spelling chose check for both the bank paper and the examining sense.
items.cn: 美式拼写用 check 兼指支票与查验之义。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects examining and controlling words.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收查验与控制类词。

entries.definition: The side of the face.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「脸颊」，读音与 check 相近。

entries.definition: A stick for writing on boards.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「粉笔」，拼写与 check 相近。

entries.definition: A list used for checking things.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「核对清单」，由 check 派生。

entries.definition: To look at something carefully.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「仔细检查」，与 check 相近。

entries.definition: To check something officially.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「视察；检视」，与 check 相近。

entries.definition: To keep something within limits.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「控制」，与 check 的遏制义相近。

normalIntro.cn: 借助词根与词族记忆 check。

abstract.en: Picture a king in chess frozen by the threat.
abstract.cn: 想象象棋里的王被威胁定格在原地。

abstract.en: Hear the referee's sharp call stopping the game.
abstract.cn: 仿佛听见裁判一声厉呼暂停了比赛。

abstract.en: Feel the pencil ticking items one by one on a list.

examples.cn: 交卷前请核对答案。

examples.en: The nurse checked my temperature and height.

examples.en: Exercise keeps weight in check.

intro.cn: check 经由象棋把波斯语「王」一词带入日常英语。

He won with a quick checkmate.

definition_zh: 人口；全体居民；种群；（统计）总体
definition_en: the people living in a place, or any group of individuals counted together, including a breeding group of animals or a complete set of data
core_image: 一张城市鸟瞰图，屋顶密密麻麻，每个小点代表一个人，远处还有一片标着虫鸟的林子
scene: 这座小城的人口在二十年间翻了一倍，供水却始终没跟上。 The city's population doubled in twenty years, and the water supply never caught up.
sceneCN: 这里 population 是「人口、居民总数」（第 1 个义项：某地居民的整体数量）；句意：这座城市的人口在二十年间翻了一番，供水却始终没跟上。图中可辨识物件：密集屋顶、代表居民的小点、远处的林地与鸟群；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 人口；全体居民；种群；总体

senses.title: People counted together
senses.definition: the total number of people who live in a particular area, town or country
senses.definitionCN: 居住在某一地区、城镇或国家的总人数
senses.example: The population of the region passed five million last year.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的人口去年突破五百万。
senses.why: populus in Latin meant 'the people'. The suffix -ation turns the body of people into a countable quantity, so the word names people as a number.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 populus 意为“人民”。后缀 -ation 把一群人变成可计数的量，因此这个词把“人”命名为一个数字。

senses.title: The people themselves
senses.titleCN: 全体居民：住在那里的人
senses.definition: all the inhabitants of a place, thought of as a social body rather than as a statistic
senses.definitionCN: 某地的全部居民，被视为一个社会群体而非一个统计数字
senses.example: The new bus route mainly serves the rural population.
senses.exampleCN: 这条新公交线路主要服务农村居民。
senses.why: English often uses population for the living community, not merely its size. The same word shifts from number to people by context alone.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用 population 指活生生的社区，而不只是它的规模。同一个词凭语境从“数字”滑向“人群”。

senses.title: A named subgroup
senses.titleCN: 特定人群：某类人构成的那一群
senses.definition: a particular group within a larger community, such as students, patients or workers
senses.definitionCN: 较大社区中的某一特定群体，如学生、病人或劳动者
senses.example: The clinic serves a mainly elderly population.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所主要服务老年人群。
senses.why: Any bounded group can be called a population because the word only requires a set of individuals and a shared boundary.
senses.whyCN: 任何有边界的群体都可称作 population，因为这个词只要求“一群个体”加“一条共同边界”。

senses.title: Biology: one breeding group
senses.definition: in biology, a group of organisms of the same species living in one area and able to interbreed
senses.definitionCN: 生物学上指同一物种、生活在同一区域且能相互交配繁殖的一群生物
senses.example: The island population of finches has been isolated for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 岛上的雀鸟种群已隔离了几个世纪。
senses.why: Biologists borrowed the demographic word and replaced 'citizens' with 'individuals of one species'. The boundary, not the species, defines the group.
senses.whyCN: 生物学家借用了人口学的词，把“公民”换成“同一物种的个体”。界定群体的是边界，而不是物种。

senses.title: Statistics: the whole set
senses.titleCN: 统计学：总体（与样本相对）
senses.definition: in statistics, the complete set of items from which a sample is drawn
senses.definitionCN: 统计学上指被抽样的完整集合，与“样本”相对
senses.example: The sample was chosen randomly from a population of ten thousand firms.
senses.exampleCN: 样本是从一万家企业的总体中随机抽出的。
senses.why: Statistics keeps the demographic sense of 'everyone', then applies it to any complete set: once you can count a group, the group is a population.
senses.whyCN: 统计学保留“全部人”的人口学含义，再套到任何完整集合上：只要能计数一群，这群就是总体。

senses.title: Animal or plant numbers
senses.titleCN: 动植物数量：一个地区的个体量
senses.definition: the number of animals or plants of a kind in a given area, often studied as density or trend
senses.definitionCN: 某一地区某类动植物的个体数量，常以密度或变化趋势来研究
senses.example: The wolf population fell sharply after the hard winter.
senses.exampleCN: 严冬之后狼的数量大幅下降。
senses.why: The counting frame is the key: pick a place and a kind, and the word reports how many are inside it.
senses.whyCN: 关键在于计数框：选定一个地方和一个种类，这个词就报告框里有多少个。

senses.title: The act of settling
senses.titleCN: 迁入定居：使地方有人住（旧义）
senses.definition: the act of filling an area with inhabitants, now mostly expressed by the related verb
senses.definitionCN: 使某地住满居民的行为，现多由相关动词表达
senses.example: The population of the frontier took three generations.
senses.exampleCN: 边疆的移民定居用了三代人的时间。
senses.why: The suffix -ation can name an action as well as a result. This older sense survives in the verb populate and in historical writing.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ation 既能命名结果，也能命名动作。这个较旧的义项保留在动词 populate 与历史写作中。

senses.title: A demographic problem
senses.titleCN: 人口结构：政策讨论里的对象
senses.definition: the size and age structure of a society considered as an economic or political issue
senses.definitionCN: 把社会的规模与年龄结构当作经济或政治问题来看待
senses.example: An ageing population puts pressure on pensions and hospitals.
senses.exampleCN: 人口老龄化给养老金和医院带来压力。
senses.why: Once governments began counting citizens for policy, population became a problem to be managed, not just a fact to be reported.
senses.whyCN: 当政府开始为政策清点公民，population 就从“被报告的事实”变成“待管理的问题”。

intro.en: Population comes from Latin populus 'the people' through populatio 'a peopling, a laying waste'. The word entered English in the 16th century on the Latin stem populatio(n-).
intro.cn: population 经由拉丁语 populatio“使人居住；蹂躏”上溯到 populus“人民”。16 世纪以拉丁词干 populatio(n-) 进入英语。

items.en: populus meant 'the people' as a body. Its deeper origin is uncertain; it may come from Etruscan, and no reliable Latin root can be given, so the deeper layer should be marked as uncertain in origin.
items.cn: populus 指作为整体的“人民”。其更深来源不确定，可能来自伊特鲁里亚语，无法给出可靠的拉丁词根，因此更深一层应标注“来源不确定”。

items.en: populatio in classical Latin could mean both 'a peopling, settlement' and 'a devastating, laying waste'. The two senses seem to come from two verbs that looked alike.
items.cn: 古典拉丁语中 populatio 既可指“使人定居”，也可指“蹂躏、毁坏”。两个义项似乎来自两个外形相近的动词。

items.en: English takes the word in the 1500s first as 'the peopling of a place', then quickly as 'the number of inhabitants'.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪先取“使地方有人居住”之义，随后很快转为“居民数量”。

items.en: With the growth of censuses in the 18th and 19th centuries, population becomes the standard word for an official count of residents.
items.cn: 18 至 19 世纪人口普查兴起，population 成为官方居民统计的标准用词。

items.en: In the 20th century biology adopts the word for any interbreeding group, transferring the census idea from citizens to individuals of one species.
items.cn: 20 世纪生物学借用该词指任何能相互繁殖的群体，把人口普查的思路从公民转到同一物种的个体。

items.en: Statistics completes the abstraction: the population is now any complete set from which a sample is drawn.
items.cn: 统计学完成了抽象化：population 现在指任何被抽样的完整集合。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the popul- shape and the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group shares the idea of people or counted individuals but differs in what is being counted.
note.cn: 形近组共享 popul- 外形与同一拉丁词干；近义组都涉及“人”或“被计数的个体”，差别在计数对象。

entries.definition: full of people, densely inhabited. It describes a place, while population names the people or their number.
entries.definitionCN: 人口稠密的；住满人的。它描述地方，而 population 命名人或其数量。

entries.definition: to fill an area with people or animals. It names the act that produces a population.
entries.definitionCN: 居住于；使有人居住。它命名产生 population 的那个动作。

entries.definition: liked by many people. It goes back to populus too, but through the sense 'of the people', not through counting them.
entries.definitionCN: 受欢迎的。它同样上溯到 populus，但走的是“属于人民的”这条义线，而不是计数。

entries.definition: the people who live in a place. It names them directly, while population can mean either the people or their count.
entries.definitionCN: 居民。它直接命名人，而 population 既可指人也可指数量。

entries.definition: people with legal membership in a state. It is a legal category, while population is a demographic count that includes non-citizens.
entries.definitionCN: 公民。它是法律范畴，而 population 是包含非公民的人口统计。

entries.definition: a group linked by shared place or interests. It stresses relationships, while population stresses mere co-presence and number.
entries.definitionCN: 社区；群体。它强调关系，而 population 强调共同在场与数量。

entries.definition: the statistical structure of a population, such as age and income. It analyses a population rather than naming it.
entries.definitionCN: 人口结构。指年龄、收入等统计构成，是对 population 的分析而非命名。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: popul- is the stem of Latin populus 'people', so population and popular sit in the same family.
normal.cn: popul- 是拉丁 populus“人民”的词干，所以 population 与 popular 同属一族。

normal.en: The -ation suffix turns people into a countable quantity, which is why the word collocates with growth, density and decline.
normal.cn: -ation 后缀把“人”变成可计量的量，所以这个词常与增长、密度、下降搭配。

normal.en: population density is arithmetic made visible: people divided by area.
normal.cn: 人口密度就是可视化的算术：人数除以面积。

normal.en: In biology the census frame is kept but the citizens become finches, wolves or trees.
normal.cn: 生物学保留了普查的计数框，只把公民换成了雀鸟、狼或树木。

normal.en: In statistics population is the whole set, and sample is the part taken from it.
normal.cn: 统计学里总体是全集，样本是从中取出的部分。

abstract.en: Picture a map covered with dots, then zoom in until each dot becomes a face.
abstract.cn: 想象一张布满小点的地图，再放大到每个点变成一张脸。

abstract.en: Picture a census form that asks one question only: how many of you are there?
abstract.cn: 想象一张只问一个问题的普查表：你们有多少人？

abstract.en: Picture a jar of seeds: the jar is the statistical population, the handful you test is the sample.
abstract.cn: 想象一罐种子：罐子是统计总体，抓出来试的一把是样本。

examples.en: Population growth slowed once the factories closed.
examples.cn: 工厂关闭后，人口增长放缓了。

examples.en: The study tracked a population of six hundred patients over five years.
examples.cn: 该研究在五年间追踪了六百名患者组成的人群。

examples.en: Statisticians distinguish the population from the sample drawn out of it.
examples.cn: 统计学家把总体与从中抽取的样本区别开来。

dict_mnemonic.text: “泡皮溜”音近 population：一群人泡在水里、皮都溜滑——人多得像下饺子 → population 人口

root: 拉丁 populus“人民”（更深来源不确定，可能出自伊特鲁里亚语）；populatio(n-) 词干 + -ation 名词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all answer one question with different boundaries: how many are inside this frame?
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在回答同一个问题，只是换边界：这个框里有多少？

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a map of dots, each dot a person.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张由小点构成的地图，每个点是一个人。

branches.en: COUNT AND BODY: the number and the living community are one word seen twice, once as arithmetic and once as society.
branches.cn: 数字与群体：数量与活生生的社区是同一个词的两种看法，一是算术，一是社会。

branches.en: NAMED SUBGROUP: students, patients and workers each get their own population once a boundary is drawn.
branches.cn: 特定人群：一旦画出边界，学生、病人、劳动者各自成一个人群。

branches.en: NON-HUMAN COUNT: breeding groups and wildlife numbers apply the census frame to other species.
branches.cn: 非人类计数：繁殖群体与野生动物数量把普查的框套到其他物种上。

branches.en: STATISTICAL WHOLE: the population is whatever complete set a sample is taken from.
branches.cn: 统计总体：population 就是任何被抽样的完整集合。

branches.en: PROCESS AND POLICY: settling an area and managing an ageing society are the verb side and the political side of the same noun.
branches.cn: 过程与政策：让人定居与管理老龄化社会，是同一名词的动词面与政治面。

intro.en: Population is the Latin stem popul- plus -ation. The suffix marks a result or an action, and the same stem yields the adjective populous and the verb populate.
intro.cn: population 是拉丁词干 popul- 加 -ation。后缀标记结果或动作，同一词干还产出形容词 populous 与动词 populate。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family runs from populus 'people' to populatio 'settlement, devastation' and populosus 'full of people'. English keeps popul- throughout.

definition_zh: 打电话；呼喊；称呼；短暂拜访
definition_en: to telephone someone, to say something loudly, to give a name to someone, or to visit someone briefly
core_image: 一只手把手机贴在耳边
scene: 晚饭后，她给外婆打了个电话。 After dinner she called her grandmother.
sceneCN: 这里 call 是「打电话」（第 1 个义项：用电话与人联系）；句意为晚饭后她给外婆打了个电话。

pos.zh: 动词：打电话；呼喊；称呼；拜访

derivatives.zh: 由 call 加 -er 构成，义为「打电话的人；来访者」
由 call 加 -ing 构成，义为「使命；天职」
由 re- 加 call 构成，义为「回想起；召回」

senses.title: To telephone someone
senses.definition: to speak to someone by phone
senses.definitionCN: 用电话与某人说话
senses.example: After dinner she called her grandmother.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭后她给外婆打了个电话。
senses.why: Early telephones needed an operator to call out a name, and that act gave the word its modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 早期电话要由接线员喊出对方的名字，这个动作让这个词有了今天的电话义。

senses.title: To say something loudly
senses.definition: to shout or say something in a loud voice
senses.definitionCN: 大声喊出或说出某事
senses.example: He called my name across the street.
senses.exampleCN: 他在街对面喊我的名字。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply to raise the voice, which is where the word began.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思就是提高嗓门，这正是这个词的起点。

senses.title: To give someone a name
senses.definition: to use a particular name or word for someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 用某个名字或词来指称某人某物
senses.example: Everyone calls him Tom.
senses.exampleCN: 大家都叫他汤姆。
senses.why: Calling out a name turned into the fixed name itself, so the verb came to mean to name.
senses.whyCN: 喊出一个名字逐渐变成固定的称呼，于是动词又有了命名的意思。

senses.title: To visit briefly
senses.definition: to make a short visit to a person or place
senses.definitionCN: 到某人处或某地作短暂停留
senses.example: We called on our neighbours after lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 午饭后我们去看望了邻居。
senses.why: A call was once a short stop on a journey, and the visit sense grew from that.
senses.whyCN: call 原指旅途中的短暂停留，拜访义由此发展而来。

intro.en: Call came from Old Norse kalla, to cry out, and the sound of a raised voice is still at its centre.
intro.cn: call 来自古诺斯语 kalla，意思是大声喊，提高嗓门的动作至今仍是它的核心。

items.en: Kalla meant to cry out or summon someone by voice.
items.cn: kalla 意为大声喊叫或用声音把某人叫来。

items.en: Old English ceallian carried the same shouting sense.
items.cn: 古英语 ceallian 带着同样的喊叫义。

items.en: Middle English callen widened to naming and summoning.
items.cn: 中古英语 callen 扩展到命名与召唤。

items.en: When the telephone arrived, calling someone came to mean ringing them.
items.cn: 电话出现后，call 某人开始表示给他打电话。

items.en: Today call covers a shout, a name, a phone ring and a short visit.
items.cn: 今天 call 涵盖喊叫、称呼、打电话和短暂拜访。

root: call 来自古诺斯语 kalla，意思是大声喊，古英语 ceallian 也带着同样的喊叫义。中古英语 callen 把用法扩展到命名与召唤，于是喊出一个名字就变成了固定的称呼。电话出现后，人们要先「叫」通对方才能说话，call 又添了打电话的意思；旅途中短暂停留的旧义则留下「拜访」这一层。今天这个词同时覆盖喊叫、称呼、打电话和短暂拜访。

sensesIntro.en: The four senses of call all grow from one picture: a voice sent out to reach someone.

definition_zh: 装饰；布置；装修；授勋
definition_en: to make something look more beautiful by adding things to it
core_image: 给房间挂上彩带和星星的人
scene: 新年快到了，教室里大家忙着布置。 We decorate the classroom with paper lanterns and red banners.
sceneCN: 这里 decorate 是「装饰」（第 1 个义项：加东西让更好看）；句意是我们用纸灯笼和红色条幅装饰教室。

derivatives.zh: 由 decorate 变词尾加 -ion 构成，义为「装饰；装饰品」
由 decorate 加 -ive 构成，义为「装饰性的」
由 decorate 加 -or 构成，义为「装饰者；室内装修师」

senses.title: To add beautiful things
senses.definition: to add pretty things to make a place or object more beautiful
senses.definitionCN: 添加漂亮的东西使场所或物品更美观
senses.example: We decorate our desks with paper flowers on Teachers' Day.
senses.exampleCN: 教师节我们用纸花装饰课桌。
senses.why: A plain thing invites little touches of colour and shine.
senses.whyCN: 平淡的东西呼唤色彩与亮光的点缀，添上它们便是装饰。

senses.title: To paint and fix a house
senses.definition: to paint the inside of a room or repair it to look nice
senses.definitionCN: 粉刷房间内部或修整使其好看
senses.example: Dad wants to decorate the kitchen this weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 爸爸想这个周末把厨房装修一下。
senses.why: A bigger project is decoration for a whole room.
senses.whyCN: 从贴几张贴纸到粉刷整间屋子，是同一个「变好看」愿望的放大版。

senses.title: To give an honour
senses.definition: to give someone a medal as an honour
senses.definitionCN: 授予某人奖章以示嘉奖
senses.example: The brave firefighter was decorated by the city.
senses.exampleCN: 那位勇敢的消防员受到市政府嘉奖。
senses.why: A medal is a decoration you can wear, so honouring used the same word.
senses.whyCN: 奖章本身就是可佩戴的装饰物，给英雄佩戴勋章便借用了装饰的词。

intro.en: Decorate comes from a Latin word for making something fit and fine.
intro.cn: decorate 来自拉丁语中表示「使合宜而漂亮」的词。

items.en: Decus meant honour or beauty; decorare meant to adorn and grace.
items.cn: 拉丁语 decus 意为荣誉、美好；decorare 意为妆点、使优美。

items.en: Decorum, proper behaviour, grew from the same family of looking right.
items.cn: 表示体面的 decorum 也出自同一「得体好看」词族。

items.en: The word reached English through Latin learning in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 该词约于十五世纪经拉丁学识传入英语。

items.en: It came to mean adding beauty to rooms, cakes and trees.
items.cn: 现代英语中它指为房间、蛋糕、树木增添美感。

items.en: Military medals gave it the honour sense still used today.
items.cn: 军功章赋予它沿用至今的授勋义。

scene: 孩子用力荡着秋千。 The child pushed the swing high into the air.
sceneCN: 这里 swing 是「秋千」（第 3 个义项）；句意：孩子把秋千推得很高。

senses.title: To move back and forth
senses.definition: to move backwards and forwards from a fixed point
senses.definitionCN: 从固定点来回移动
senses.example: The lamp swung in the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 灯在风中摇摆。
senses.why: The hanging seat gave the word its basic picture of motion around a pivot.
senses.whyCN: 悬挂的座位给这个词提供了绕支点运动的基本画面。

senses.title: To turn sharply
senses.definition: to turn quickly in a particular direction
senses.definitionCN: 朝某方向迅速转动
senses.example: She swung round to face him.
senses.exampleCN: 她转身面对他。
senses.why: A swinging object changes direction, so a person turning quickly is described the same way.
senses.whyCN: 摆动的物体改变方向，于是迅速转身的人也用同样的说法。

senses.title: A seat on ropes
senses.definition: a seat hanging from ropes that a person rides for fun
senses.definitionCN: 用绳索吊起供人玩耍的座位
senses.example: The children queued for the swing.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们排队等秋千。
senses.why: The noun names the very object whose motion produced the verb.
senses.whyCN: 名词指的正是产生这个动词的那种物体。

senses.title: A shift in opinion
senses.definition: a change from one position or opinion to another
senses.definitionCN: 从一种立场或观点转向另一种
senses.example: There was a swing towards the opposition.
senses.exampleCN: 出现了倒向反对派的转变。
senses.why: A pendulum moves to the other side, so a change of opinion is pictured as a swing.
senses.whyCN: 钟摆摆向另一边，于是观点的改变被画成一次摆动。

intro.en: Swing comes from an old Germanic verb for beating or swinging.
intro.cn: swing 源自古老的日耳曼语动词，意为挥打或摆动。

items.en: The root described a sweeping, swinging movement.
items.cn: 该词根描述挥扫、摆动的动作。

items.en: Swingan meant to beat or flog.
items.cn: swingan 意为击打或鞭打。

items.en: Swingen widened to any back and forth motion.
items.cn: swingen 扩展到任何来回运动。

items.en: Swing named the hanging seat children ride.
items.cn: swing 指孩子们玩的悬挂座位。

items.en: Swing extended to shifts of opinion and mood.
items.cn: swing 又扩展到观点与情绪的变化。

note.en: Swing is compared with look-alike words and with words for moving to and fro.
note.cn: 把 swing 与形近词以及表示来回移动的词作比较。

normalIntro.cn: swing 指绕悬点的运动，后指任何转向另一边的变化。

abstract.en: A swing is a promise that what goes up comes back.
abstract.cn: 秋千是一种承诺：上去的终会回来。

abstract.en: Opinion swings like a pendulum, never resting long.
abstract.cn: 舆论像钟摆一样摆动，从不久停。

abstract.en: To swing is to give your weight to something outside you.
abstract.cn: 荡秋千就是把重量交给身外之物。

sensesIntro.cn: swing 涵盖来回摆动、悬挂座椅以及转向另一边的变化。

core.en: Motion around a fixed point, always returning.
core.cn: 绕固定点运动，总会返回。

intro.cn: swing 可构成 swings、swinging、swung 与形容词 swinging。

latinIntro.en: Swing is Germanic; Latin pendere, to hang, gives pendulum.
latinIntro.cn: swing 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 pendere（悬挂）衍生出 pendulum。

items.meaning: to move from side to side
items.example: The trees sway in the breeze.

latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 pendere 意为悬挂。

definition_zh: 向前；前进；提前； forwards 的形容词：前面的；先锋的；发送；转交
definition_en: toward the front or ahead in time; situated in front; to send something on to another person
core_image: 身体前倾迈步：重心移向正前方
scene: 足球课上，教练大声指挥队员把球传向球门方向。 The coach shouted, 'Pass the ball forward!'
sceneCN: 这里 forward 是「向前」的意思（第 1 个义项：朝前移动）；教练要求队员把球传向对方球门方向。

derivatives.zh: forward 加名词后缀，义为「早熟；冒进」
forward 加 -ly，义为「在前方；冒失地」
forward 的英式变体，义为「向前」，副词专用
反义方位词，义为「之后；后来」

senses.title: Toward the front in space or time
senses.definition: toward a place or time ahead of the present position
senses.definitionCN: 朝空间前方或时间前方移动。
senses.example: Please move forward so others can get on the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 请往前走，让别人能上车。
senses.why: For- means forward in time or front, and -ward marks direction.
senses.whyCN: for- 表示「在先、在前」，-ward 后缀标记方向。

senses.title: Situated near the front; advanced
senses.definition: placed near the front, or developing earlier than usual
senses.definitionCN: 位置靠前的，或发展得比一般早的。
senses.example: The forward engine of the plane took the impact.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机前部的发动机承受了撞击。
senses.why: The direction word becomes a position word.
senses.whyCN: 方向词变成位置词。

senses.title: To send on to another address or person
senses.definition: to pass a letter, message, or email on to someone else
senses.definitionCN: 把信件、消息或电子邮件转给别人。
senses.example: I forwarded your message to the class group.
senses.exampleCN: 我把你的消息转发到了班级群。
senses.why: Pushing something forward reaches the next person.
senses.whyCN: 把东西往前送，就送到了下一个人手里。

senses.title: A player who leads the attack
senses.definition: in sports, a player who plays near the opponent's goal
senses.definitionCN: 球类运动中靠近对方球门、主攻得分的队员。
senses.example: He plays as a forward in the school football team.
senses.exampleCN: 他在校足球队里踢前锋。
senses.why: The attacker stands forward of the team, closest to the goal.
senses.whyCN: 进攻队员站在全队最前方、离球门最近的位置。

intro.en: Forward is a native English compound of for- and -ward, two very old direction elements.
intro.cn: forward 是本土复合词，由 for- 与 -ward 两个极古老的方位成分构成。

items.en: For- meant 'in front, going before', seen in forefather and foremost.
items.cn: for- 意为「在前、先行」，见于 forefather、foremost。

items.en: -weard meant 'turned toward', the ancestor of -ward.
items.cn: -weard 意为「转向」，是 -ward 的祖先。

items.en: Foreweard meant the front part or earlier period.
items.cn: foreweard 指前部或更早的时期。

items.en: Forward and forwards split uses: adjective and verb favored forward, pure adverb often forwards.
items.cn: forward 与 forwards 分工：形容词、动词多用 forward，纯副词常见 forwards。

items.en: The email sense and business senses like look forward to became universal.
items.cn: 转发邮件义和 look forward to 等商务用法普及开来。

note.en: Words that look like forward and words of direction and sending.
note.cn: 与 forward 形近的词及表示方向、转发的词。

entries.definition: the adverb twin of forward, preferred in British English
entries.definitionCN: 向前；forward 的副词孪生形，英式英语更常用。

entries.definition: an introduction to a book; often confused with forward
entries.definitionCN: 书的序言；与 forward 仅一字母之差，易混。

entries.definition: a prize; shares the -ward ending but not the for- part
entries.definitionCN: 奖品；共享 -ward 词尾，与 forward 词义不同。

entries.definition: in front or earlier
entries.definitionCN: 在前面；提前；与 forward 的方向义近义。

entries.definition: continuing forward in time or space
entries.definitionCN: 继续向前；同含 -ward 后缀。

entries.definition: to pass on a message
entries.definitionCN: 转达、传递；与 forward 的转发义近义。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on direction, position, and the look forward to pattern.
normalIntro.cn: 围绕方向、位置与 look forward to 句式的五条记忆钩子。

normal.en: Split forward into for (front) + ward (toward): moving to the front.
normal.cn: 拆成 for（前）+ ward（朝向）：朝前方移动。

normal.en: Learn the fixed pattern: look forward to + doing.
normal.cn: 记住固定句式：look forward to + 动名词。

normal.en: Distinguish foreword (a book's preface) from forward (ahead).
normal.cn: 区分 foreword（序言）与 forward（向前）。

normal.en: In football, the forward is the front player nearest the goal.
normal.cn: 足球里 forward 是离球门最近的前锋。

normal.en: Forward an email = push the message onward to the next person.
normal.cn: 转发邮件就是把消息继续往前送。

abstract.en: Picture a runner leaning forward before the starting gun.
abstract.cn: 想象发令枪响前前倾起跑的选手。

abstract.en: Picture an envelope passed hand to hand along a line.
abstract.cn: 想象信封沿一排人手手相传。

abstract.en: Picture a clock hand jumping forward one hour.
abstract.cn: 想象时针向前拨快一小时。

examples.en: We are all looking forward to the school trip next week.
examples.cn: 我们都很期待下周的学校旅行。

examples.en: Could you forward this email to the head teacher?
examples.cn: 你能把这封邮件转发给校长吗？

examples.en: The car rolled slowly forward along the narrow lane.
examples.cn: 汽车沿着窄巷缓缓向前滚动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「福特德」——福特车向前开：forward 就是车头所指的方向。

root: forward 为古英语复合词：for-（前、先，见 forefather）+ -weard（朝向，见 -ward）。字面即「朝前」。英式副词变体 forwards；同根方位词有 backward、onward、afterward。

sensesIntro.en: Forward spans direction, position, transmission, and the attacking player role.
sensesIntro.cn: forward 横跨方向、位置、转发传递与球类运动的前锋角色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: body weight shifting toward what is ahead
core.cn: 核心意象：重心移向前方

branches.en: Movement toward the front in space
branches.cn: 空间上朝前方移动

branches.en: Moving an event to an earlier time
branches.cn: 把事情提前到更早的时间

branches.en: Standing at the front of a group or machine
branches.cn: 位于群体或机器的前部

branches.en: Pushing a message onward to the next person
branches.cn: 把消息继续传给下一个人

branches.en: The front position in an attacking line-up
branches.cn: 进攻阵容中的最前位置

intro.en: Forward combines the front element for- with the direction suffix -ward.
intro.cn: forward 由「前」成分 for- 与方向后缀 -ward 组合而成。

latinIntro.en: The -ward family is Germanic, so the cognates are all native direction words.
latinIntro.cn: -ward 词族属日耳曼来源，同源词都是英语本土方位词。

items.example: A forefather is one who came before.

items.exampleCN: 副词加 -s 的英式习惯。

items.example: The author wrote a short foreword.
items.exampleCN: 与 forward 同源成分、不同含义。

items.example: I look forward to seeing you.

definition_zh: 博物馆；陈列馆；馆藏机构；专门展室
definition_en: a building where objects of artistic, historical or scientific interest are collected, studied and shown to the public, and also the institution or collection itself
core_image: 玻璃柜里一排旧陶罐，被一盏小灯照出细密的裂纹
scene: 展厅里灯光压得很低，孩子们贴着玻璃柜找一只陶罐上的裂缝，讲解员说它在地下埋了很久。 The city museum keeps a whole floor of pottery that was found beneath the old market.
sceneCN: 这里是「博物馆」（第 1 个义项：收藏并陈列文物或艺术品的场所）；句意为这座市立博物馆留出整整一层，陈列旧市场地下挖出的陶器。图中可辨识物件：玻璃柜、陶罐、射灯。

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语 mousa（缪斯）与 -logy（学说）构成，义为「博物馆学」
由 museology 加表示「人」的后缀 -ist 构成，义为「博物馆学专家」
与 museum 同源于缪斯，义为「沉思；冥想」

senses.title: A building that collects and displays objects
senses.definition: a building where objects of art, history or science are collected, kept and shown to the public
senses.definitionCN: 收藏、保存并向公众展示艺术、历史或科学物品的建筑
senses.example: The museum opens at nine and closes at five.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆九点开门，五点闭馆。
senses.why: Greek mouseion was a place of the Muses, a seat of learning, and the modern word still names a building that holds knowledge rather than sells goods.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 mouseion 是缪斯女神的地方，也就是治学之所；现代这个词仍指收藏知识的建筑，而不是卖东西的场所。

senses.title: The institution or collection itself
senses.definition: the institution, or the collection it holds, considered apart from its building
senses.definitionCN: 把这个机构或它收藏的藏品单独来看，而不指建筑本身
senses.example: The museum lent three paintings to a show in another city.
senses.exampleCN: 这家博物馆把三幅画借给了另一座城市的展览。
senses.why: Because the collection travels while the building stays, the name moved from the place to the body that owns and cares for the objects.
senses.whyCN: 藏品可以出借巡展，而建筑留在原地，于是这个名称从「地方」转到「拥有并照管这些藏品」的机构。

senses.title: A room devoted to a special subject
senses.definition: a room or gallery set apart for a particular subject, often smaller than a full museum
senses.definitionCN: 为一个特定主题单独辟出的房间或展廊，通常比完整的博物馆小
senses.example: A small museum of typewriters sits above the bookshop.
senses.exampleCN: 书店楼上有一间小小的打字机陈列室。
senses.why: When the gathering of objects was small and focused, English kept the same word for a single room, so a museum can be a cabinet-sized space for one subject.
senses.whyCN: 当收藏的对象又少又专时，英语仍用同一个词指单个展室，所以 museum 也可以是为一个主题办的小小空间。

intro.en: Museum goes back to the Greek mouseion, a place of the Muses, and it reached English through Latin and French as a name for a place of study.
intro.cn: museum 可追溯到希腊语 mouseion，即缪斯之地；它经拉丁语与法语进入英语，最初指治学之所。

items.en: Mousa, a Muse, named one of the goddesses of poetry, music and learning, and their shrines were places of the arts.
items.cn: mousa 即缪斯，是掌管诗歌、音乐与学问的女神，供奉她们的地方就是艺术之地。

items.en: Mouseion meant a place dedicated to the Muses, a seat of learning where books and objects were kept and discussed.
items.cn: mouseion 意为献给缪斯的地方，是保存并讨论书籍与器物的治学之所。

items.en: Latin borrowed mouseion as museum, keeping the sense of a study or a place of learned pursuits.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 mouseion 借作 museum，仍指书房或治学之所。

items.en: French musée carried the word into the language of galleries, where it named a place holding a collection open to visitors.
items.cn: 法语 musée 把这个词带进画廊的语言，指收藏并向参观者开放的地方。

items.en: Modern English fixes the idea of a public building, and the Greek word for Muse survives inside muse and music.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义固定为公共建筑，希腊语中「缪斯」这个词仍留在 muse 与 music 里面。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the Greek Muse and on the place ending -eum; the near-meaning group collects places and events that hold collections.
note.cn: 形近组收由希腊语「缪斯」与表地点的 -eum 词尾构成的词；近义组收收藏与展示藏品的场所和活动。

entries.definition: To think deeply about something, or a source of inspiration; the word shares the Greek Muse.
entries.definitionCN: 沉思，或灵感的来源；与希腊语缪斯同源。

entries.definition: Sounds arranged to be sung or played; the name comes through the Muses.
entries.definitionCN: 为歌唱或演奏而组织的声音；名称经由缪斯而来。

entries.definition: A picture made of small coloured pieces; the shape is close but the origin differs.
entries.definitionCN: 用小块彩色材料拼成的图画；字形相近，但词源不同。

entries.definition: A large, grand tomb; the ending looks alike but the word comes from a king's name.
entries.definitionCN: 宏伟的陵墓；词尾形似，但这个词来自一位国王的名字。

entries.definition: A room or building where art is shown.
entries.definitionCN: 陈列艺术品的房间或建筑。

entries.definition: A public display of objects or works.
entries.definitionCN: 公开展示物品或作品的活动。

entries.definition: A place or collection of records kept for study.
entries.definitionCN: 为研究保存档案的地方或收藏。

entries.definition: A group of objects gathered and kept together.
entries.definitionCN: 收集并放在一起的一组物品。

normalIntro.en: A Greek place of the Muses became a Latin study, a French gallery and an English public building; the entry follows that journey.
normalIntro.cn: 一个希腊的缪斯之地，先后变成拉丁语的书房、法语的画廊、英语的公共建筑；这个词条就沿着这条路展开。

normal.en: Mouseion was a place of the Muses, so a museum is first of all a home for knowledge, not a shop.
normal.cn: mouseion 是缪斯之地，所以 museum 首先是知识的住所，而不是店铺。

normal.en: The Muses cover poetry and music too, which is why muse and music sit in the same word family.
normal.cn: 缪斯也掌管诗歌与音乐，所以 muse 与 music 留在同一个词族里。

normal.en: -Eum is a place ending borrowed from Greek, so museum, mausoleum and gymnasium share a shape that marks a location.
normal.cn: -eum 是从希腊语借来的地点词尾，所以 museum、mausoleum、gymnasium 共有一个表示场所的形状。

normal.en: English keeps museum for the building, while a gallery can be a single room and a collection can travel.
normal.cn: 英语用 museum 指建筑，而 gallery 可以只是单个房间，collection 则可以出借巡展。

normal.en: Natural history museum joins the word with a subject, which shows the building can be named after what it holds.
normal.cn: natural history museum 把词与一个主题连起来，说明这类建筑可以用所藏之物来命名。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp over a glass case, one cracked pot lit from above.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯照在玻璃柜上，一只裂了缝的陶罐被光从上方照亮。

abstract.en: A place named after goddesses of art suggests that objects are kept so they can be read, not merely stored.
abstract.cn: 一个以艺术女神命名的地方，说明藏品被保存下来是为了供人解读，而不只是堆放。

abstract.en: The word began with study and ended with visitors, so a museum is learning made public.
abstract.cn: 这个词从治学开始，以观众收尾，所以博物馆就是把学问向公众打开。

examples.en: The museum was closed for repairs all summer.
examples.cn: 这座博物馆整个夏天都在维修，暂停开放。

examples.en: We spent a rainy afternoon in the natural history museum.
examples.cn: 下雨的下午，我们待在自然史博物馆里。

examples.en: The museum lent its best painting to a foreign exhibition.
examples.cn: 这家博物馆把最好的一幅画借给了国外的展览。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「缪泽姆」——缪斯女神住的地方，如今成了博物馆；记住 museum。

root: 希腊语 mousa（缪斯）→ mouseion（缪斯之地，治学之所）→ 拉丁语 museum → 法语 musée → 英语 museum；同族词有 muse、music、museology，没有另立的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a place of the Muses; the senses divide into the public building, the institution and its collection, and a single room for one subject.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是缪斯之地；义项分出公共建筑、机构与馆藏，以及为单一主题设的展室。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit glass case holding one cracked pot, with a guide and children in front of it.

latinIntro.en: Latin passed on the Greek place word as museum, so the Latin forms here are borrowings rather than native relatives.

senses.title: Four-sided shape
senses.definition: a shape with four equal sides and four right angles
senses.definitionCN: 四条边相等、四个角都是直角的图形
senses.example: She drew a square on the board.
senses.exampleCN: 她在黑板上画了一个正方形。
senses.why: This is the concrete shape sense.

senses.title: Open city space
senses.definition: an open area in a town, often with buildings around it
senses.definitionCN: 城镇中四周常有建筑的开阔场地
senses.example: The children flew kites in the square.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在广场上放风筝。
senses.why: The shape became a place in old towns.
senses.whyCN: 在古老城镇里，方形的地块变成了场所。

senses.title: Product of a number
senses.definition: the result of multiplying a number by itself
senses.definitionCN: 一个数自乘所得的结果
senses.example: Five squared is twenty-five.
senses.exampleCN: 五的平方是二十五。
senses.why: A square number is drawn as a square array.
senses.whyCN: 平方数可以排成正方形点阵。

senses.title: Fair and honest
senses.definition: honest and fair in dealing with people
senses.definitionCN: 待人处事诚实公平的
senses.example: It was a square deal for both sides.
senses.exampleCN: 这对双方都是公平的交易。
senses.why: A right angle suggests straight and fair conduct.
senses.whyCN: 直角象征正直、公平的行为。

intro.cn: square 经古法语 esquarre 来自拉丁语 exquadrare，意为使成方形。

items.cn: exquadrare 意为使成方形。

items.en: Esquarre meant a square or a rule.
items.cn: esquarre 意为方形或曲尺。

items.en: Square named the shape and the tool.

items.en: The open place sense grew in towns.
items.cn: 「广场」义项在城镇中发展起来。

items.en: The fair sense came from honest measure.
items.cn: 「公正」义项来自诚实的度量。

note.en: Square is compared with look-alike words and words for open places.
note.cn: 把 square 与形近词以及表示开阔场地的词作比较。

normal.en: Fold the paper into a square.

abstract.en: A square deal needs two honest sides.
abstract.cn: 公平的交易需要双方都诚实。

abstract.en: Every number can grow into a square.

root: 经古法语 esquarre 来自拉丁语 exquadrare（使成方形），词根 quadr- 表示四；由「四边相等的图形」引申出广场、平方和公正。

sensesIntro.en: Square names a shape, a town space, a product of multiplication, or fair conduct.

branches.cn: 圆点排成整齐的方阵。

intro.cn: square 构成复数、比较级、副词和名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is exquadrare, to make square.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁语源头是 exquadrare，意为使成方形。

definition_zh: 服从；听从；遵守；遵从
definition_en: to do what a person, a rule or a force tells you to do, or to act in the way it requires
core_image: 一只脚已经迈出去，又被收回到别人指定的位置上
scene: 祠堂的院子里，长辈把香递到年轻人手里，只说了该站的位置，没有再解释。 The young man obeyed and stepped back two paces without a word.
sceneCN: 这里 obeyed 是「服从、听从」（第 1 个义项：按有威权的人的要求行动）；句意为年轻人照做，一言不发地退后两步。图中可辨识物件：祠堂院子、递出的香、后退的脚步。

derivatives.zh: 由 obey 的名词词干加后缀 -ence 构成，义为「服从；顺从」
由拉丁分词词干加形容词词尾 -ent 构成，义为「顺从的；听话的」
由 obedient 加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「顺从地」
由否定前缀 dis- 加 obey 构成，义为「不服从；违抗」
由 dis- 加 obedience 构成，义为「不服从」

senses.title: Doing what a person in authority asks
senses.definition: to do what someone with authority over you tells you to do, even when you would rather not
senses.definitionCN: 按有权威的人的要求去做，哪怕自己并不情愿
senses.example: The soldiers obeyed every order without question.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们毫无质疑地服从每一道命令。
senses.why: Latin oboedire was built from ob-, toward, and audire, to hear; obey therefore begins as leaning your ear toward a voice and letting it decide your next move.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 oboedire 由 ob-（朝向）加 audire（听）构成，所以 obey 的起点是把耳朵朝向一个声音，并让它决定你下一步怎么走。

senses.title: Acting according to a rule or law
senses.definition: to act in the way that a law, rule or set of instructions requires
senses.definitionCN: 按照法律、规则或一套指示所要求的方式行事
senses.example: Every driver must obey the speed limit on this road.
senses.exampleCN: 每位司机在这条路上都必须遵守限速。
senses.why: Once the voice that must be heard belongs to a written rule instead of a person, the same yielding turns into keeping the law, which is why obey fits a captain and a statute alike.
senses.whyCN: 当那个必须听从的声音从一个人变成一条写下来的规则，同样的「让位」就变成守法；所以 obey 既能跟长官，也能跟法条。

senses.title: Following what an inner feeling urges
senses.definition: to act on what a feeling, instinct or urge tells you to do
senses.definitionCN: 按照某种感觉、本能或冲动的要求行动
senses.example: She obeyed her instincts and turned back before the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 她听从直觉，在桥前折了回来。
senses.why: The one who gives the order can also sit inside you, so the verb stretches from an outer voice to an urge that feels like a command.
senses.whyCN: 下命令的人也可以坐在你身体里，于是这个动词从外面的声音延伸到一种像命令一样的冲动。

senses.title: Of a thing, answering a control
senses.definition: of a machine, ship or system, to move or work in the way a control or force directs it
senses.definitionCN: 指机器、船只或系统按操控或外力的方向运转
senses.example: The old boat obeyed the helm even in rough water.
senses.exampleCN: 这条旧船即使在浪里也随舵转向。
senses.why: A ship that answers the wheel is described as if it heard a command, which is how a word about human listening comes to describe machines that respond smoothly.
senses.whyCN: 一艘随舵转向的船，被说成像听见了命令；一个本来讲人「听」的词，就这样用来描述机器顺滑的响应。

intro.en: Obey travels from Latin through French; its Latin core joins a prefix meaning toward to a verb meaning hear, so the word begins with listening.
intro.cn: obey 经法语来自拉丁语，其拉丁核心是「朝向」的前缀加「听」的动词，所以这个词从「听」开始。

items.en: Audire meant to hear, and it supplied the sense of hearing that still hides inside this word.
items.cn: audire 意为听见，为这个词提供了藏在内部的「听」这一层意思。

items.en: Oboedire joined ob-, toward, with audire, so it meant to listen to and comply with a person who had the right to be heard.
items.cn: oboedire 把表示朝向的 ob- 与 audire 合在一起，意为听从、顺从一个有权被听见的人。

items.en: Old French obeir kept the sense of submitting to a person and passed the verb into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 obeir 保留「顺从某人」的意思，在诺曼时期之后把动词传入英语。

items.en: Middle English obeien widened from obeying a person to obeying a rule, an order or a promise.
items.cn: 中古英语的 obeien 从服从一个人，扩展到遵守规则、命令或承诺。

items.en: Modern English also lets instincts, limbs and machines obey, while obedience and disobey keep the family together.
items.cn: 现代英语还让本能、肢体和机器也「服从」；obedience 与 disobey 把这个词族拢在一起。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin root for hearing and the family built on it; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of yielding to authority.
note.cn: 形近组沿着「听」这条拉丁词根及其词族；近义组收表示让位于权威的动词。

entries.definitionCN: 按吩咐行事的举动；服从。

entries.definition: Willing to do what one is told.
entries.definitionCN: 愿意按吩咐行事的；顺从的。

entries.definition: To refuse to do what a rule or person requires.

entries.definition: Loud or clear enough to be heard.
entries.definitionCN: 响度或清晰度足够被听见的。

To accept the authority of another person.

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin sum of toward plus hear, so its family keeps returning to who is speaking and who is listening.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「朝向」加「听」的一次相加，所以词族反复绕着「谁在说、谁在听」转。

normal.en: Oboedire joins ob-, toward, and audire, to hear, so to obey is first of all to turn your ear toward a voice.
normal.cn: oboedire 把表示朝向的 ob- 与表示听的 audire 合起来，所以服从首先是让耳朵朝向一个声音。

normal.en: The opposite is disobey, built with the negative prefix dis-, and the noun behind it is disobedience.
normal.cn: 反义形式是 disobey，用否定前缀 dis- 构成；它背后的名词是 disobedience。

normal.en: Obedient keeps the same Latin stem but adds -ent, the ending of an adjective, so the word becomes a quality of the person.
normal.cn: obedient 保留同一拉丁词干，加上形容词词尾 -ent，于是变成人的一种性质。

normal.en: Obedience is the noun, ending in -ence, and it names the state of being willing to listen.
normal.cn: 名词 obedience 以 -ence 收尾，指愿意倾听的那种状态。

normal.en: Obey often takes orders, rules or the law as its object, because what it follows is whatever has the right to be heard.
normal.cn: obey 常以 orders、rules 或 law 作宾语，因为它所跟从的，是那个有权被听见的东西。

abstract.en: Every act of obedience is a small choice to let another voice steer your feet.
abstract.cn: 每一次服从，都是让另一个声音来拨动自己的脚。

abstract.en: The prefix here points at a voice and the rest of the word is an ear; authority lives in that short distance.
abstract.cn: 这个词的前缀指向一个声音，其余部分是一只耳朵；权威就住在这段短短的距离里。

abstract.en: A ship that obeys the helm shows how far the word has travelled, from a person listening to wood turning in water.
abstract.cn: 一艘随舵转向的船说明这个词走了多远：从一个人倾听，到木头在水里转动。

examples.en: The soldiers obeyed every order without question.
examples.cn: 士兵们毫无迟疑地服从每一道命令。

examples.en: Every driver must obey the speed limit on this road.
examples.cn: 每位司机在这条路上都必须遵守限速。

examples.en: She obeyed her instincts and turned back before the bridge.
examples.cn: 她听从直觉，在桥前折了回来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我必」——长官开口，我必照做；obey 就是服从。

root: 一般认为来自拉丁语 oboedire（听从），由 ob-（朝向）加 audire（听）构成，经古法语 obeir 进入英语；同族词多与「听、顺从」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is turning your ear to a voice; the senses divide by who speaks, from a person with authority to a written rule, to an inner urge, and finally to a machine that answers a control.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是把耳朵转向一个声音；义项按「说话者是谁」分开：有威权的人、写下来的规则、内心的冲动，最后是随操控响应的机器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot already stepping out, then pulled back to the place someone else has set.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只脚已经迈出去，又被收回到别人指定的位置上。

branches.en: a soldier stepping back into line at a word
branches.cn: 士兵听见一句话，退回队列

branches.en: a driver slowing down where the sign says so
branches.cn: 司机在有标志的地方减速

branches.en: a woman turning back because something inside said so
branches.cn: 她因为心里有个声音而回头

branches.en: a tiller answering the hand of the one at the wheel
branches.cn: 舵柄顺着掌舵人的手转动

branches.en: one will bent first to a rule, then to a machine
branches.cn: 同一份顺从，先交给规则，后交给机器

intro.en: The word carries a Latin prefix meaning toward and a Latin verb meaning to hear, and its English family grows through endings for state and for quality.
intro.cn: 这个词带着表示「朝向」的拉丁前缀与表示「听」的拉丁动词，它的英语词族靠表示状态与性质的后缀长出来。

latinIntro.en: Latin audire, to hear, and its compound oboedire, to listen and comply, are the recorded ancestors of this word family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 audire（听）及其复合词 oboedire（听从）是这个词族有记录的祖先。

definition_zh: 历史的；历史学的；历史题材的；历史上真实存在的
definition_en: relating to history or to the past, based on records of past events, or existing in the past rather than only in imagination
core_image: 一只戴白手套的手翻动发黄的档案，纸边压着一枚旧印章
scene: 一部小说把故事放进真实存在过的朝代，但主角是虚构的。 The novel is set in a historical period, but its main character never existed.
sceneCN: 这里 historical 是「与历史有关的」（第 1 个义项：基于史实的）；小说以真实朝代为背景。

pos.zh: 历史的；历史学的；历史题材的；历史上真实存在的（多作定语）

derivatives.zh: 有历史意义的；历史性的

senses.title: Relating to history
senses.titleCN: 历史的：与历史这门学问有关
senses.definition: relating to history as a field of study or to the study of past events
senses.definitionCN: 与作为研究领域的历史，或与对过去事件的研究有关
senses.example: The department publishes work on historical method.
senses.exampleCN: 该系发表关于历史方法的成果。
senses.why: history comes from Greek historia 'inquiry'; historical marks what belongs to that inquiry rather than to the present.
senses.whyCN: history 出自希腊 historia“探究”；historical 标记属于这一探究、而非当下的事物。

senses.title: Set in a past period
senses.titleCN: 历史题材的：以某一过去时期为背景
senses.definition: of a novel, film or exhibition, set in an earlier period and built from its details
senses.definitionCN: 指小说、影片或展览以较早时期为背景，并依其细节构建
senses.example: The museum's historical reconstruction shows a street of nineteen-twenties shops.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆的历史复原展示了一条二十世纪二十年代的店铺街。
senses.why: A period setting borrows the record for atmosphere, so the adjective distinguishes it from stories set today.
senses.whyCN: 时期设定借用历史记录来营造氛围，这个形容词因此把它与以当代为背景的故事区分开。

senses.title: Real in the past
senses.titleCN: 历史上真实存在的：确有其人与其事
senses.definition: existing or happening in the real past rather than being invented
senses.definitionCN: 在真实的过去存在或发生，而非虚构
senses.example: The character is historical; the love affair is invented.
senses.exampleCN: 这个人物是历史上真实存在的，那段恋情则是虚构的。
senses.why: When the adjective contrasts with fiction, it certifies that the record, not the imagination, is the source.
senses.whyCN: 当这个形容词与虚构相对时，它确认来源是记录而非想象。

senses.title: Based on records
senses.titleCN: 基于史料的：有据可查的
senses.definition: supported by documents, evidence and scholarly sources
senses.definitionCN: 有文献、证据与学术来源支持的
senses.example: The claim is historical in the sense that two ledgers support it.
senses.exampleCN: 这一说法有史料依据，因为有两本账簿支持它。
senses.why: History is an evidence-based discipline, so the adjective can assert that documentation exists.
senses.whyCN: 历史是一门以证据为基础的学科，因此这个形容词可以断言文献确实存在。

senses.title: Studying change over time
senses.titleCN: 历时演变的：研究时间上的变化
senses.definition: in linguistics and other fields, studying a subject across its development rather than at one moment
senses.definitionCN: 在语言学等领域，研究某对象随时间的演变，而非某一时刻的状态
senses.example: Historical linguistics traces how the vowel shifted over four centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 历史语言学追踪这个元音在四百年间如何变化。
senses.why: The adjective names a method, not just a subject: the historical view compares stages of a single thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词命名的是方法，而不只是对象：历史的视角比较同一事物的各个阶段。

senses.title: Protected for its age
senses.titleCN: 有历史价值的：因年代而受保护
senses.definition: of a building or site, valued and often legally protected for its age and associations
senses.definitionCN: 指建筑或场所因年代与关联而受重视、常受法律保护
senses.example: The house is listed as historical and cannot be altered without permission.
senses.exampleCN: 这座房子被列为历史建筑，未经许可不得改动。
senses.why: Age becomes value when a community decides to keep a place, and the adjective carries that legal weight.
senses.whyCN: 当社区决定保留某地时，年代便成了价值，这个形容词便承载了那份法律分量。

senses.title: Original cost in accounting
senses.titleCN: 历史成本的：按取得时的价格记账
senses.definition: in accounting, valued at the price originally paid rather than at current market value
senses.definitionCN: 会计中按最初支付的价格而非当前市价计量
senses.example: The land is carried at historical cost, far below its market value.
senses.exampleCN: 这块土地按历史成本入账，远低于其市价。
senses.why: Accounting keeps the past in its books: the price at purchase is a fact about then, so the adjective marks that fixed record.
senses.whyCN: 会计把过去留在账上：购入时的价格是关于“当时”的事实，这个形容词标记的正是这一固定记录。

senses.title: Belonging to earlier times
senses.titleCN: 往昔的：属于过去而非现在
senses.definition: belonging to an earlier time and no longer current
senses.definitionCN: 属于较早时期、如今已不再通行
senses.example: Historical prices look absurdly low beside today's figures.
senses.exampleCN: 与今天的数字相比，往昔的价格低得离谱。
senses.why: The simplest reading is just 'of the past'; everything else in the word's range grows from that plain contrast with now.
senses.whyCN: 最简单的读法就是“属于过去的”；该词其余用法都从这一与“现在”的朴素对照生长出来。

intro.en: Historical is history plus -ical, from Greek historia 'inquiry' through Latin and French. It exists beside the shorter historic, with a different sense. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: historical 是 history 加 -ical，源自希腊 historia“探究”，经拉丁与法语传入。它与较短的 historic 并存，但含义不同。年代为约数。

items.en: historia meant 'inquiry, investigation, written account', from histōr 'witness'. The deeper origin of histōr is uncertain and often discussed.
items.cn: historia 意为“探究、调查、书面记述”，出自 histōr“见证者”。histōr 的更深来源不确定，学界多有讨论。

items.en: Latin historia covered both narrative and knowledge of events. Old French estoire gave English history in the 13th century, while story came from the same source by another route.
items.cn: 拉丁 historia 兼指叙述与对事件的了解。古法语 estoire 于 13 世纪给出英语 history，而 story 经另一路径同源而来。

items.en: English formed historic in the 17th century and historical in the 16th. For a long time they were interchangeable.
items.cn: 英语于 16 世纪构成 historical，17 世纪构成 historic。很长一段时间内二者可互换。

items.en: In the 18th and 19th centuries usage settled: historic means 'important in history', historical means 'relating to history or occurring in the past'.
items.cn: 18 至 19 世纪，用法逐渐固定：historic 意为“在历史上重要的”，historical 意为“与历史有关的或发生在过去的”。

items.en: Historical linguistics, historical cost and historical record fixed the adjective in technical writing during the 19th and 20th centuries.
items.cn: 历史语言学、历史成本与历史记录在 19 至 20 世纪把该形容词固定于技术写作中。

items.en: The origin of Greek histōr is disputed, and the exact date when historic and historical stopped being interchangeable varies by source.
items.cn: 希腊 histōr 的来源有争议；historic 与 historical 不再可互换的确切年代，各家说法不一。

note.en: The first group turns on the historic/historical distinction; the second contains adjectives about the past and about records.
note.cn: 第一组聚焦 historic 与 historical 的区别；第二组是关于过去与记录的形容词。

entries.definition: Meaning 'important enough to be remembered'. A historic speech changes events; a historical speech merely happened in the past.
entries.definitionCN: 意为“重要到值得被记住”。historic speech 改变事态；historical speech 只是发生在过去的演讲。

entries.definition: The adverb of historical. It answers 'when' or 'from what standpoint', not 'how important'.
entries.definitionCN: historical 的副词；回答“何时”或“从什么立场”，而非“多重要”。

entries.definition: A person who studies or writes history. It is a person noun, not a description of a period.
entries.definitionCN: 研究或撰写历史的人；是人物名词，不描述某个时期。

entries.definition: in a state of uncontrolled emotion, unrelated meaning
entries.definitionCN: 情绪失控的，拼写音近但意义无关

entries.definition: Relating to earlier time in general, with no implication of records or scholarship.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指较早时间，不暗示记录或学术。

entries.definition: Relating to archives and stored documents; narrower than historical, which also covers events and methods.
entries.definitionCN: 关于档案馆与所存文献；比 historical 窄，后者还覆盖事件与方法。

entries.definition: Based on or consisting of documents, or a factual film; it stresses the evidence form rather than the past itself.
entries.definitionCN: 以文献为依据或由文献构成，或指纪实影片；强调证据形式而非过去本身。

entries.definition: Handed down by custom rather than recovered from records; it describes continuity, not documentation.
entries.definitionCN: 由习俗传承而非从记录中复原；描述的是延续性，而非文献性。

entries.definition: Old and valued as an object; it applies to things, especially furniture, not to periods or methods.
entries.definitionCN: 古老而作为器物受珍视；多用于物品尤其家具，不用于时期或方法。

normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: history + -ical: belonging to history.
normal.cn: history + -ical：属于历史的。

normal.en: historical context, historical record and historical novel are the standard collocations.
normal.cn: 历史背景、历史记录、历史小说是标准搭配。

normal.en: The family is history, historical, historic, historically, historian, historiography.
normal.cn: 同族词是 history、historical、historic、historically、historian、historiography。

normal.en: historical is the neutral adjective; historic claims importance. Test with 'important': if it fits, use historic.
normal.cn: historical 是中性形容词，historic 声称重要性。可用“重要”来测：若说得通就用 historic。

normal.en: historical cost is an accounting term; do not read it as 'cost in history'.
normal.cn: historical cost 是会计术语，不要读成“历史上的成本”。

abstract.en: Picture a gloved hand turning a page of a ledger that has yellowed for two hundred years.
abstract.cn: 想象一只戴手套的手翻动一页泛黄两百年的账簿。

abstract.en: Picture a film set built from photographs, where every chair matches the year in the caption.
abstract.cn: 想象一处依据照片搭起的场景，每把椅子都与说明中的年份相符。

abstract.en: Picture the same word written in five centuries on one sheet, each hand changing the vowels.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个词在五个世纪里写在同一张纸上，每一笔都改动元音。

examples.en: Historical evidence for the treaty is thin: three letters and one seal.
examples.cn: 关于这项条约的史料很单薄：三封信和一枚印章。

examples.en: The film is historical in its costumes but fictional in its plot.
examples.cn: 这部影片在服装上是历史的，情节却是虚构的。

examples.en: Historical linguistics explains why the spelling no longer matches the sound.
examples.cn: 历史语言学解释了为什么拼写不再与读音相符。

root: 希腊 historia“探究、记述”← histōr“见证者”；拉丁 historia、古法语 estoire → history + -ical。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses cluster around one idea, the recorded past, and then spread into genre, evidence, method, protection, accounting and simply 'then'.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个观念——被记录的过去——展开，随后延伸到体裁、证据、方法、保护、会计，以及朴素的“当时”。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gloved hand turning a yellowed page stamped with an old seal.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只戴手套的手翻动盖着旧印章的泛黄书页。

branches.en: DISCIPLINE AND EVIDENCE: the field and its documentary basis are the same back-and-forth.
branches.cn: 学科与证据：这门学问与其文献基础是同一套往返。

branches.en: PERIOD AND TRUTH: a setting in the past and a person who really lived both appeal to the record for authority.
branches.cn: 时期与真实：以过去为背景与确有其人，都向记录借取权威。

branches.en: METHOD: the historical view compares stages instead of freezing one moment.
branches.cn: 方法：历史的视角比较各阶段，而非冻结某一时刻。

branches.en: KEEPING THE PAST: heritage listing and historical cost both fix an earlier value into the present.
branches.cn: 留住过去：遗产登录与历史成本都把较早的价值固定进当下。

branches.en: PLAIN 'THEN': the simplest sense, from which the specialized ones branch.
branches.cn: 朴素的“当时”：最简单的义项，其余专门义项由此分支。

intro.en: Historical is history plus -ical. The Greek root historia passed through Latin and French before reaching English.
intro.cn: historical 是 history 加 -ical。希腊词根 historia 经拉丁与法语才进入英语。

latinIntro.en: The historia family in English includes history, story, historical, historic, historian and historiography; the look-alike histrionic belongs to a different Latin word.
latinIntro.cn: 英语中的 historia 词族包括 history、story、historical、historic、historian、historiography；形近的 histrionic 则出自另一个拉丁词。

items.meaning: the recorded past or its study
items.meaningCN: 被记录的过去或其研究

items.example: Historiography asks who was left out of the record.
items.exampleCN: 史学史追问谁被排除在记录之外。

items.meaningCN: 叙述；history 的同源双重借词

definition_zh: 生气的；愤怒的；发怒的
definition_en: feeling strong displeasure about something
core_image: 男孩握紧拳头盯着被弄坏的模型
scene: 男孩握紧拳头，盯着被弄坏的模型。 He was angry about the broken model.
sceneCN: 这里 angry 是「生气的」（第 1 个义项：因某事感到不快）；句意为他对被弄坏的模型很生气。

senses.title: Feeling displeasure
senses.definition: feeling unhappy and upset about something
senses.definitionCN: 因某事感到不快与烦恼
senses.example: She was angry about the broken window.
senses.exampleCN: 她为被打破的窗子生气。
senses.why: The old root meant narrow or painful, and a mind pressed tight by displeasure is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 古词根意为狭窄、痛苦，心里被不快压紧，就是第一义。

senses.title: Filled with strong rage
senses.definition: showing strong, heated displeasure
senses.definitionCN: 显出强烈而激烈的怒气
senses.example: The crowd grew angry at the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 人群因延误而愤怒起来。
senses.why: The same tight feeling pushed to full strength becomes rage rather than mild displeasure.
senses.whyCN: 同一种被挤紧的感觉推到最强，就从轻微不快变成愤怒。

intro.en: The recorded history of angry is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 angry 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: The old word meant grief or trouble.
items.cn: 古词意为悲伤或烦恼。

items.en: The same root also suggested something narrow and tight.
items.cn: 同一词根还带有狭窄、紧绷的意味。

items.en: Middle English used it for a person full of displeasure.
items.cn: 中古英语用它形容满心不快的人。

items.en: English kept both the grief and the heated sense.
items.cn: 英语十四世纪同时保留悲伤与激烈两种意味。

items.en: Today it usually means upset about a person or a thing.
items.cn: 今天它通常指对某人或某事感到不快。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definition: An informal word for very angry.

entries.definition: A strong word for very great anger.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的说法，指极度愤怒。

normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词形、真实的词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.cn: 古词根意为狭窄：愤怒就是心里被不快挤紧。

normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 anger 与 angrily。

normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 angry 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: feeling strong displeasure about something.
normal.cn: 当你想表达「生气的」时用它。

definition_zh: 因为；从…以来
definition_en: from a past time until now, or because
core_image: 一条从过去延伸到现在的时间线
scene: 自从搬到海边，她的睡眠好多了。 Since moving to the coast, she has slept much better.

senses.title: From a past time until now
senses.definition: starting at a past point and continuing to the present
senses.definitionCN: 从过去某点开始并持续到现在
senses.example: Since moving to the coast, she has slept much better.
senses.exampleCN: 自从搬到海边，她的睡眠好多了。

senses.title: Because

senses.whyCN: 从先前事实推出原因，便有了「因为」。

senses.title: Before now

senses.definitionCN: 在现在之前某时，属较旧用法

senses.exampleCN: 他很久以前就离开了。
senses.why: The adverb kept a small separate life.

items.cn: 十七世纪英语借入 laboratory，指做化学与物理工作的房间。

items.en: British speech shortens it to lab, and American use puts the stress on the first syllable.
items.cn: 英式口语把它缩为 lab，美式则把重音放在第一音节。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word spreads from chemistry to psychology, language study and industry.
items.cn: 二十世纪里这个词从化学扩展到心理学、语言教学与工业。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words sharing the Latin work root and forms of this word; the near-meaning group gathers other places of study and work.
note.cn: 形近组收共享拉丁语「劳动」词根的词与本词的形式；近义组收其他学习与工作场所。

entries.definition: The everyday clipping of laboratory.
The Latin work root in its other English form, meaning toil or workers.
entries.definitionCN: 同一拉丁语词根的另一英语形式，指劳作或劳工。

entries.definition: Built on the same work root, meaning worked out in great detail.
entries.definitionCN: 同出该词根，义为「精心制作的」。

entries.definition: A room with tools for making, not for controlled experiment.
entries.definitionCN: 放工具做制作的房间，不是做受控实验的。

entries.definition: A place built to watch the sky, named after looking rather than working.
entries.definitionCN: 为观测天空而建的地方，以「看」而非「做」命名。

entries.definition: An organisation for research or teaching, larger than one room.
entries.definitionCN: 研究或教学机构，规模大于一个房间。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root, the British and American stress, and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用真实的拉丁语词根、英美重音差别，以及这个词常见的搭配。

normal.en: Laboratory is built on laborare, to work, so it is a room for work.
normal.cn: laboratory 建立在 laborare（工作）之上，所以是为了干活而设的屋子。

normal.en: Alchemists had laboratories before scientists did.
normal.cn: 炼金术士比科学家更早拥有实验室。

normal.en: British speakers say it with four beats, American speakers with three.
normal.cn: 英式读音是四个音节，美式是三个。

normal.en: Laboratory equipment and laboratory test are the standard pairings.
normal.cn: laboratory equipment 与 laboratory test 是标准搭配。

normal.en: The lab is the same word with the middle taken out.
normal.cn: lab 就是这个词挖掉中间的那一截。

abstract.en: A laboratory is a place where the world is made small enough to question.
abstract.cn: 实验室是把世界缩小到可以被追问的地方。

abstract.en: The name means only workroom, yet the work inside keeps turning guesses into evidence.
abstract.cn: 它的名字只意味着「工作间」，里面的事却不断把猜测变成证据。

abstract.en: Any place built to test a claim, from a clinic to a city, now borrows this name.
abstract.cn: 任何为检验主张而建的地方，从诊所到城市，如今都借用这个名字。

examples.en: The samples are analysed in a licensed laboratory.
examples.cn: 样本在具备资质的实验室里分析。

examples.en: The laboratory moved into a larger building last year.
examples.cn: 这个实验室去年搬进了更大的楼里。

examples.en: Laboratory work takes a third of the course.
examples.cn: 实验工作占这门课程的三分之一。

dict_mnemonic.text: labor 劳动 + -atory 场所——干活的地方，就是实验室

root: 拉丁语 laborare（工作、劳作）派生名词 laboratorium（干活之所），中世纪拉丁语中用于炼金术的工作室；十七世纪英语借入，指科学实验场所，后缩略为 lab，并扩展至心理学、语言教学与工业研究。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the equipped room, the building or research unit it grew into, and the practical work carried on there.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：配备仪器的房间，由它扩展而成的整栋建筑或研究单位，以及在那里进行的实验工作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: long benches under cold lights, instruments waiting to be used.
core.cn: 核心意象：冷白灯光下的长台，仪器等着被使用。

branches.en: THE ROOM LINE: a space fitted with apparatus for tests.
branches.cn: 房间线：为检测而装设仪器的空间。

branches.en: THE BUILDING LINE: the name grows to a whole research unit.
branches.cn: 建筑线：名字可扩展到整个研究单位。

branches.en: THE ACTIVITY LINE: the place stands for the work done in it.
branches.cn: 活动线：场所代表在其中所做的工作。

branches.en: THE ROOT LINE: laborare makes the word a workroom by origin.
branches.cn: 词根线：laborare 让这个词在原义上就是工作间。

branches.en: THE SHORT LINE: the clipping lab is now the everyday form.
branches.cn: 简短线：缩略形式 lab 已成日常说法。

intro.en: Laboratory is a Latin place noun whose family in English is mainly the clipping, plus a few formal derivatives.
intro.cn: laboratory 是拉丁语场所名词，其英语词族主要是截短形式与少数正式派生词。

latinIntro.en: Latin labor, laborare, laboratorium and elaborare are all recorded, so nothing here is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 labor、laborare、laboratorium 与 elaborare 均有记录，故此无构拟成分。

items.example: The laboratory is quiet at night.
The noun is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是整族的源头。

items.example: It marks a laboratory for research.
items.exampleCN: 它标明用于研究的实验室。

latinEntries.meaning: to work out, to take pains
